lines.trans: Look at page one, Mr Lukas: conversion into offices next month. All over and done!
One moment, did you also read page two clipped behind it?
Only small grey numbers! At page one my heart already stopped!
Look where Lukas is pointing with his pencil, Martin!
Clause fourteen of the Leipzig Old Quarter bylaw, and my brother outside is nodding!

lines.trans: In plain words, please! What does Clause fourteen mean?
No courtyard building over eighty years old may turn private if a neighbourhood café opens downstairs daily.
Open daily for neighbours, like a public morning café?!
Exactly! Right now your four tables only serve your own overnight guests.

words.gloss: to host, serve (food and drink to)

lines.trans: Wait, if we open our courtyard gate every morning for coffee and rolls...
Then the city protects your lease for another ten years!
Martin! Now your glasses just slipped off your nose from pure joy!
